sections.overview: Gunning’s golden mole is a South African member of the golden mole family, Chrysochloridae.
sections.identification: It is one of two species in the genus Neamblysomus; published species-specific descriptions are sparse.
sections.habitat: The species is known from Limpopo Province in northeastern South Africa, where it inhabits montane forest and grassland.
sections.diet: The sources consulted provide too little species-specific evidence to describe its diet reliably.
sections.behavior: Like other golden moles, it is adapted to a largely subterranean, burrowing way of life.
sections.reproduction: Species-specific reproductive observations were not established in the sources consulted.
sections.ecology: Its restricted range links the species to montane habitats in a region where golden moles face increasing habitat degradation.
sections.conservation: The Mammal Diversity Database reports an Endangered IUCN assessment from 2024; the limited range makes habitat change a conservation concern.
